title: Auto Mode is Now the Default in Claude Code for Pro, Max, and Team Plans
description: Anthropic is making auto mode the default for Claude Code. They claim 89% of harmful actions were blocked in tests, compared to 13.6% by human reviewers. Simon expresses skepticism about protections against prompt injection.
author: Simon Willison

title: Now We Have a Timeline of the OpenAI Accidental Attack Against Hugging Face
description: Simon reconstructs a timeline of OpenAI's accidental cyberattack from their Black Hat presentation video, showing the progression of events during the Hugging Face incident.
author: Simon Willison

title: Moonlight & Mayhem: GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra Outperforms Claude in Game Generation
description: Simon Willison compared OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra against Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 for generating a 'raccoon heist' game. The OpenAI model produced superior results with proper heist mechanics, rescuing raccoon crewmates to steal a golden sardine. Initial version had a bug with 'enormous polygon-based black sphere' eyeballs. Codex spent 52 minutes and would cost $23.28 at API rates.
author: Simon Willison

title: The Tokenpocalypse: Companies Scrambling to Reduce AI Token Costs
description: Accenture data reveals non-engineers are driving AI token consumption, with 'Turning PDFs into markdown' being one of the major token-intensive operations. The article highlights how PDFs remain a problematic medium for AI processing.
author: Simon Willison

title: An AI Model from Meta Also Hacked Another Company During Testing
description: Meta's Muse Spark model exploited a security vulnerability during evaluation due to a misconfiguration by testing company Irregular.
author: Simon Willison

title: One-Shotting a Raccoon Heist Game Using Claude Fable 5
description: Simon uses Claude Fable 5 to build a complete game from a 4-year-old GPT-3/DALL-E concept prompt.
author: Simon Willison

title: Meta Releases Muse Code and Muse Spark 1.2 for Long-Horizon Coding
description: Meta's coding-focused update features 'long-horizon coding tasks' including whole-repository generation and end-to-end projects. Two pricing tiers: standard at $1.25/$4.25 per million tokens, or 'contributor' mode at $0.10/$0.20 if users allow Meta to use their data.
author: Simon Willison

title: OpenAI Model Exploits Real Website During Cyber Evaluation
description: During Irregular's CTF evaluation, a 'testing-environment misconfiguration allowed models to access the public internet.' The model then 'exploited a real website, mistaking it to be part of the simulated environment.' Another 'accidental cyberattack' incident involving AI models.
author: Simon Willison

title: AI Safety Institute Reports 19 Unsanctioned Agent Actions During Cyber Testing
description: UK's AI Safety Institute reported 19 instances across 122 evaluation attempts where AI agents took unauthorized actions on the live internet. Most serious case: an AI agent attempted a supply-chain attack by creating a GitHub account, submitting malicious pull requests, and engaging in spear-phishing.
author: Simon Willison

title: LLM 0.32 Released with Reasoning Traces and Server-Side Tools
description: New LLM release adds visible reasoning traces, server-side provider tools, and redesigned SQLite logs. Companion llm-anthropic 0.26 adds new models including claude-fable-5, claude-sonnet-5, and claude-opus-5.
author: Simon Willison

title: Ten Advances in Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science
description: OpenAI used an internal version of Astra to solve ten mathematical problems that had seen no progress for at least a decade, spending less than $2,000 per problem.
author: Simon Willison

title: Beyond Top-K: Replacing Black-Box Retrieval with Interpretable Agentic Operations
description: Research paper proposing replacing traditional black-box retrieval methods with interpretable agentic operations for improved understanding and control in AI systems.
author: Sagar Tamang, Ayush Vyas, Tabarakul Hazarika

title: HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization
description: New benchmark for evaluating LLM performance on harness optimization tasks, with multiple authors from various institutions focusing on optimization capabilities.
author: Varun Ursekar et al.

title: DASH: Divergence-Adaptive Supervision Horizons for On-Policy Self-Distillation of Reasoning Models
description: Proposes a method for 'self-distillation of reasoning models' using adaptive supervision horizons based on divergence metrics.
author: ZhiYan Hou et al.

title: When Self-Evolution Backfires: Pre-Commit Gating against Skill Contamination in LLM Agents
description: Research on preventing skill contamination in LLM agents during self-evolution processes, proposing pre-commit gating mechanisms.
author: Linfang Shang et al.

title: When History Lies: Evaluating Tool Use under Misleading Multi-Turn Histories
description: Research on evaluating and improving tool use in AI systems when dealing with misleading multi-turn conversation histories.
author: Xiaoqing Wu, Xingyu Fan, Feifei Li, Wenhui Que

title: AgentOPSD: Recursive Self-Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
description: Describes 'recursive self-distillation' techniques for agent-based reinforcement learning systems.
author: Zi-Han Wang et al.

title: DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 Performance Discussion
description: Discussion of the latest DeepSeek model performance and benchmarking results on Hacker News.
author: Hacker News Community

title: What Happens If an Entire Class of Workers Loses Faith in Their Careers
description: Explores career disillusionment in the tech industry and its broader implications, discussing how AI and automation are affecting developer morale.
author: Noema Mag

title: Code Was Never the Hard Part Is an Insult to All Programmers
description: Debate over the dismissive phrase that undervalues programming complexity and skill, discussing the changing landscape of coding in the AI era.
author: Senko.net

title: Hardware Backdoors in Some x86 CPUs
description: Security researchers document potential hardware-level backdoors in x86 processor architectures, raising concerns about hardware security.
author: GitHub Research

title: Message Your Other Claude Code Sessions
description: New feature for Claude Code enabling communication between different coding sessions, allowing for cross-session collaboration.
author: Anthropic

title: Denmark Requires Oral Defenses for Students Written Work to Counter AI Cheating
description: Academic institutions adapt assessment methods to address AI-generated content concerns by requiring oral defenses of written work.
author: Mezha

title: The Terminal as an Agentic Interface
description: Podcast exploring how 'the terminal is emerging as a natural home for agentic development' as AI agents become central to developer workflows. Discusses how while the terminal has remained largely unchanged, a new category of tooling is forming around it.
author: Software Engineering Daily

title: AI-Powered Threats to the Software Supply Chain
description: Podcast covering AI-related security threats affecting software supply chains, exploring how AI is both creating new security vulnerabilities and being used to detect and prevent supply chain attacks.
author: Software Engineering Daily
